2_ac_measurability.evidence: §10 enumerates 17 AC IDs total. Counting parser fixtures (vitest .test.ts): AC-CR1-CODE-FENCE-PROTECTED, AC-CR1-FOOTNOTE-FENCE-PROTECTED, AC-CR1-TILDE-FENCE-PROTECTED, AC-CR1-OUTSIDE-FENCE-STILL-EXTRACTED, AC-CR1-MISMATCHED-CLOSER-NOT-CLOSING (5 CR-1), AC-CR2-DETAILS-COMPACT, AC-CR2-DETAILS-COMPACT-OPEN (2 CR-2), AC-CR1-CR2-INTERACTION (1 interaction). That is 8 vitest parser fixtures, not '5'. AC-CR3-SUB-SUP-DISTINCT is a 9th vitest fixture (or style-snapshot equivalent). But §8 M15 says '5 new fixtures + 27 prior cycle fixtures' (line 201), §11 Implementation Map says '~5 new fixtures' (line 441), §15 DoD #1 says 'All 5 new fixtures from §10 PLUS 27 prior fixtures' (line 502). This 5-vs-9 inconsistency is a real spec hole: Dev could land 5 fixtures (e.g., the simplest 5), claim PASS per the DoD wording, and still have 3-4 ACs unverified. The fix: replace '5 new fixtures' with the explicit AC-ID-by-AC-ID enumeration, OR raise the count to '~9 new fixtures'. 4_risk_analysis.evidence: §14 lists 10 risks (R1-R10). R1 catches fence-state opener-line handling, R6 catches SUMMARY_LINE_RE multi-line backward compatibility, R5 catches RN-Web transform render reality. However: (a) NO RISK enumerates the tab-indented-fence inconsistency that codex round-2 surfaced. happy-app's `tryCodeBlock` at parseMarkdownBlock.ts:207 uses `trimmed.startsWith('\`\`\`')` (verified by direct read) — meaning tab-indented or arbitrarily-indented fence lines ARE rendered as code blocks. But the BA spec's pseudo-code `extractDefinitions` uses CommonMark-strict `^ {0,3}` (line 240). A user message containing `\t\`\`\`\n[ref]: x\n\`\`\`` would be rendered as code (tryCodeBlock matches) but [ref]: x would be stripped from bodyLines because extractDefinitions did NOT enter fence state for the 1-tab-indented fence. Net effect: code block would render with content '', the [ref]: x line would be silently swallowed, regression of THE EXACT bug Cycle 9 is fixing. (b) M4 unclosed-fence guard has no R-entry and no AC fixture — meaning a fence opener with no closer + def-shaped line below would silently regress to current behavior. The risk that 'fence-state tracker leaks state across messages' or 'EOF-with-unclosed-fence preserves nothing' is not enumerated. (c) Fixture count gap (see dimension 2) implies risk that Dev under-implements ACs is not formally caught — the spec's R10 only covers 'codex round-1 caught 4 issues; codex round-2 caught 2 more' but NOT 'codex round-3 might catch under-fixturing'.

rejection_reasons.summary: Fixture-count/DoD inconsistency. Spec says '5 new fixtures / ≥32' in 3 places (§8 M15 line 201, §11 line 441, §15 DoD #1 line 502) but §10 enumerates ≥9 vitest fixtures. Dev could land 5 minimal fixtures, mark M15/§15 PASS, and leave 3-4 ACs from §10 silently unverified. The /close-debate could then surface 'we have ACs without fixtures' and CLOSE: NO — same failure pattern as Cycle 8.
rejection_reasons.concrete_fix_required: Replace every '5 new fixtures' / '≥32 fixtures' phrasing with explicit per-AC-ID enumeration of vitest fixtures: 'All 9 new vitest fixtures (AC-CR1-CODE-FENCE-PROTECTED, AC-CR1-FOOTNOTE-FENCE-PROTECTED, AC-CR1-TILDE-FENCE-PROTECTED, AC-CR1-OUTSIDE-FENCE-STILL-EXTRACTED, AC-CR1-MISMATCHED-CLOSER-NOT-CLOSING, AC-CR2-DETAILS-COMPACT, AC-CR2-DETAILS-COMPACT-OPEN, AC-CR1-CR2-INTERACTION, AC-CR3-SUB-SUP-DISTINCT) + 27 prior = ≥36 fixtures green'. Update §8 M15, §11 Implementation Map, §15 DoD #1 consistently.

rejection_reasons.summary: Tab-indented fence inconsistency unenumerated. Direct read of parseMarkdownBlock.ts:207 confirms `tryCodeBlock` uses `trimmed.startsWith('\`\`\`')` — meaning ANY-leading-whitespace fence lines render as code blocks. BA spec pseudo-code at line 240 uses CommonMark-strict `^ {0,3}` for FENCE_OPEN_RE. The two are inconsistent: a user message like `\t\`\`\`\n[ref]: x\n\`\`\`` would render as code block (tryCodeBlock matches with full trim) but extractDefinitions would NOT enter fence state (4+ leading whitespace including tab fails 0-3 space regex), so `[ref]: x` would still be stripped from bodyLines. This is the EXACT user-need bug Cycle 9 claims to fix, just with tab indentation. Spec §14 has no R-entry for it.
rejection_reasons.concrete_fix_required: EITHER (preferred): align extractDefinitions opener detection with tryCodeBlock by using `trimmed.startsWith('\`\`\`'|'~~~')` instead of `^ {0,3}` regex (renderer-consistent stance — protect what the renderer actually treats as a fence). Add fixture: tab-indented fence `\t\`\`\`\n[ref]: x\n\`\`\`` preserves [ref]: x verbatim. OR: add a §13 non-goal entry explicitly out-of-scoping tab-indented fences AND add an §14 risk acknowledging the inconsistency AND add a §17 Out-of-Scope Observation flagging this for follow-up. The renderer-consistent stance is materially better because it closes the user-need-leak; the OOS stance leaves a known regression vector in main.

rejection_reasons.summary: M4 unclosed-fence MUST has no dedicated AC fixture. Spec §8 M4 says 'when a fence is unclosed (EOF reached), all remaining lines are preserved (no def stripping inside the unclosed fence)'. But §10 has no AC for this. None of the 5 enumerated CR-1 ACs exercise unclosed fences. A Dev could implement only the closed-fence path and pass all listed ACs while still stripping def-lines from a fence-without-closer. Real coverage gap.
rejection_reasons.concrete_fix_required: Add AC to §10: `AC-CR1-UNCLOSED-FENCE-PRESERVES`: GIVEN `'\`\`\`\n[ref]: a\n[^1]: b'` (no closing fence, EOF) WHEN parsed THEN 0 link defs collected AND 0 footnote defs collected AND raw lines '[ref]: a' and '[^1]: b' preserved verbatim in bodyLines (rendered as code or text — implementation choice, but def lines NOT stripped).

rejection_reasons.summary: AC-LIVE-SUB-VS-SUP-DISTINCT at §10 line 426 only requires 'visual baseline shift differs between 2 (sub, lower) and 2 (sup, raised); screenshot evidence at desktop AND mobile'. But RN-Web translates `transform: [{translateY: ±4}]` to CSS `transform: translateY(±4px)` on the inline `<span>`/`<Text>` — which CAN produce screenshot evidence that 'looks similar' on small fonts. Without an objective DOM measurement, QA could rubber-stamp screenshots that don't actually distinguish them. Codex round-2 explicitly recommended 'DOM/bounding-box measurement or explicit screenshot crop proving sub's digit is lower and sup's digit is higher'.
rejection_reasons.concrete_fix_required: Strengthen AC-LIVE-SUB-VS-SUP-DISTINCT: add a DOM bounding-box measurement assertion. Example: 'use Playwright browser_evaluate to read the bounding rect of the sub digit and the sup digit; assert sub.top > sup.top (sub digit's top edge is below sup digit's top edge by ≥ 6px on desktop, ≥ 4px on mobile)'. This converts a subjective screenshot check to an objective measurement — prevents PASS-on-rubber-stamp-screenshot.
